bull.probability_evidence: EV/EBITDA sits at the 4th percentile of its own 5-year range and 40% below the peer median (EQT/AR/RRC/CTRA/CNX), with net debt/EBITDA low at 0.46x and Piotroski F-score 8 (research/EXE/factsheet-2026-10-08.md valuation and 'Other' tables) -- a real but not dominant re-rate case per the Bull case in research/EXE/2026-10-08-evaluation.md.

target_band.cite: Half the spread between the bull target's own EV/EBITDA basis (3.5x->4.4x 5y median, implying ~114 via EBITDA=6.776bn and net debt=3.117bn backed out from mkt cap 20.6bn and net debt/EBITDA 0.46x [factsheet-2026-10-08.md 'Other'/quality tables]) and the same proportional peer-gap closure (39.1%, matched to the EV/EBITDA peer-gap move from -40% to -24%) applied to P/E (7.6x vs 11.0x peer median -> ~8.93x, ~104) and P/FCF (8.2x vs 12.5x peer median -> ~9.88x, ~106) [factsheet-2026-10-08.md valuation table]: (114.2-103.5)/114 = 4.7%.

base.probability_evidence: The 12.14% FCF yield funds debt paydown and buybacks, but shares outstanding are up 13.24% YoY despite $850m of Q1 2026 buybacks, offsetting the per-share benefit (research/EXE/2026-10-08.md section 5); probability trimmed from an even 0.50 split by the macro overlay's small toward-bear tilt (research/EXE/2026-10-08-macro.md macro_tilt).

target_band.cite: Base case basis holds EV/EBITDA at 3.5x (research/EXE/2026-10-08-evaluation.md scenarios.base.basis); with no multiple re-rate posited, pricing the same flat scenario via P/E (7.6x) or P/FCF (8.2x) [factsheet-2026-10-08.md valuation table] implies the same ~88 current price, so the valuation anchors do not disagree.

bear.probability_evidence: The 5y ROIC trend is falling (-6.3pp) and net debt/EBITDA spiked from 0.28x to 4.42x within FY2024 alone (research/EXE/2026-10-08.md section 2), a leverage precedent now layered with the Sept 2026 $500m notes pricing (research/EXE/2026-10-08.md section 6); probability raised from 0.25 by the macro overlay's small toward-bear tilt on rising real yields and HY spreads (research/EXE/2026-10-08-macro.md macro_tilt).

target_band.cite: Half the spread between the bear target's own EV/EBITDA basis (3.5x->2.9x 5y minimum, implying ~71 via the same EBITDA/net-debt backout as the bull case) and the same proportional peer-gap widening (26.1%, matched to the EV/EBITDA peer-gap move from -40% to -50%) applied to P/E (7.6x -> ~6.72x, ~78) and P/FCF (8.2x -> ~7.08x, ~76) [factsheet-2026-10-08.md valuation table]: (77.9-70.7)/71 = 5.0%.

expected_12m_move.cite: Mixed near-term signal in mc-inputs factor_news.SPY: record highs (2026-10-06/07 Bloomberg/CNBC) alongside a tech-led rally 'masking a broader market sell-off' and bearish put-spread activity (CNBC 2026-10-07) and a pullback on rising Treasury yields (Reuters, TipRanks 2026-10-07) -- no clear direction, so 0 per house rule.

mc-inputs factor_news.IEF headlines (2026-10-01/07): '30-Year Yields Return to 2002 High', 'Global Bond Markets Sell Off on France's Fiscal Worries', 'The Bond Rout Is Deepening' -- predominantly rising-yield/falling-bond-price headlines, reinforced by the macro overlay's dominant_chain (real yields & HY spreads rising; DFII10 +61bp/3m, DGS10 +72bp/3m, research/EXE/2026-10-08-macro.md), giving a modest negative move for the bond-price factor IEF.

jumps.name: Leverage/credit shock
jumps.reason: Net debt/EBITDA rising and holding above 2.0x for two consecutive quarters is the note's first invalidation trigger; EXE's net debt/EBITDA already swung from 0.28x to 4.42x within FY2024, and it just priced a new $500m senior notes offering (Sept 2026), layering fresh leverage.
jumps.cite: research/EXE/2026-10-08.md section 4 (first bullet) and section 6 ('Unusual items')

annual_probability.cite: 1 of the 5 fiscal years (FY2021-FY2025) shown in research/EXE/factsheet-2026-10-08.md quality table had a net debt/EBITDA spike (FY2024, to 4.42x) = 1/5 = 0.20/yr.

impact.cite: Largest single-week fall in mc-inputs.json analogues.largest_falls not already used for the earnings or gas-price jumps.

jumps.name: Gas-price collapse
jumps.reason: EXE is a commodity price-taker with no moat beyond relative cost position; management's own mid-cycle assumption of $3.50-4.00/MMBtu 'to balance the market' shows the business needs a specific gas price to earn its cost of capital, and ROIC swung from 36.6% (FY2022) to -2.8% (FY2024) on gas-price moves alone.

annual_probability.cite: Only 1 of the 10 largest weekly falls in mc-inputs.json analogues.largest_falls (over ~5 years, i.e. once per 5 years) exceeds -15%.

impact.cite: Largest weekly fall in the 5-year history.

technical_tilt.cite: research/EXE/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Price section: price is -5.0% vs its 50-day MA and -10.1% vs its 200-day MA, with the 50-day MA itself -5.3% below the 200-day MA (a death cross) and 3-month momentum -1.6%; modest negative tilt, within the +/-0.02 cap, 3m horizon only.
